dialogReference.para: Area to cover. Leave blank for the current map view.
DTM: the bare-ground surface, predicted by machine learning; use it for fault mapping. DSM: the top of trees and buildings (five bands, about five times the data to stream).

Mosaic dataset: one seamless layer, best for large areas (Standard or Advanced licence). Separate layers: one layer per 1-degree tile. VRT file: one small file streaming all tiles, any licence, slower to draw zoomed out.
Connection to the bucket. Leave blank to use (or make) gem15.acs in the project's home folder.
Geodatabase for the mosaic dataset (default: the project's).
Leave blank to name it after its coordinate system (e.g. GEM15_dtm_UTM55S), so later runs in the same zone add to the same mosaic and an area in another zone gets its own.

Leave blank so tiles in one UTM zone keep their own 15 m grid. Across zones the tool picks GDA2020 / GA LCC (Australia), NZTM2000 (New Zealand) or a projection centred on your area. Choose a projected system in metres, never degrees.
Folder for the VRT file (default: the gem15 folder in the project's home folder).
Which DSM band: dsm (the surface), its 5th, 50th or 95th percentile, or dsm_std (the spread of heights within each pixel).
The rasters added (tiles or the VRT).
Also show the tiles' outlines, where seams between acquisitions can look like scarps.

summary.para: Add the GEM-15 tiles covering an extent as one mosaic dataset (referenced from the cloud), as separate layers, or as a VRT file that streams them.

usage.bullet_item: Mosaic datasets need a Standard or Advanced licence. Zoomed out over more than about 20 tiles, a mosaic shows tile outlines only: zoom in.
Nothing is downloaded up front: the layers read only what they draw.
Add a hillshade and local relief model with Terrain Stack.
